Two lists

The text’s own speech headings, in Protestant book order. Nothing here is classified as an event. A later quotation does not join or close a row.

Narrator “and YHWH said” / “and Elohim said,” then every clause of that speech until the story resumes (a wayyiqtol that is not a saying, or a new chapter). Genesis 1 “let there be” is here because the narrator says Elohim said it. GEN 3:15 is here because it sits in the speech that starts at GEN 3:14.

Clauses the text marks with prophecy vocabulary: נאם, כה אמר יהוה, דבר יהוה היה, נבא, חזון/חזות, משא with a company word, προφητ-, πληρόω with γραφή/προφήτης. Content is same-sentence or nested in the MACULA tree only. GEN 15:1 is here as a delivery (“the word came in a vision”), including “do not fear.”
